chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whichever people revive something from the land and develop it, they are more rightful with it, and it is for them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on owning land that has not been cultivated?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'ihya' al-mawat' (reviving dead land), asserting that cultivation confers ownership rights, a concept central to Shia fiqh regarding unclaimed property. It reflects the practical application of stewardship in Islamic law, where active development by an individual or community grants them priority over others, reinforcing the link between labor and ownership in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Humran, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Whichever people revive something from the land, and work upon it, so they are more rightful with it, and it is for them’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Whoever of people revive a land and build it, they are more deserving to have it and it is for them. 5 ”
